troubleshooting_steps.action: With the mouse still connected, test the touchpad to confirm it now responds alongside the mouse
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This verifies the setting change successfully allows both input devices to work at the same time

troubleshooting_steps.action: If this specific option is not available in Windows Settings, check if a manufacturer-specific touchpad utility is installed, since some laptops manage this behavior through their own software instead
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some manufacturers control the automatic disable-on-mouse-connect behavior through their own utility rather than the standard Windows settings

troubleshooting_steps.action: Within the manufacturer utility, if present, look for and disable any option that automatically turns off the touchpad when an external mouse is detected
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This achieves the same result through the manufacturer's own control panel if the standard Windows option is not available or effective

possible_solutions: Enable 'Leave touchpad on when a mouse is connected' under Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad
Check a manufacturer-specific touchpad utility for an equivalent setting
Test both devices together after adjusting the relevant setting
prevention: Adjust this setting proactively if you regularly use both a touchpad and an external mouse together
Be aware this is often a default, intentional behavior rather than a malfunction
